params.body:
The home pages showed a fixed number of posts, trends and reports, written into `HomeController`. Editors now set these amounts in the Studio. The pipeline sends them with the trends (pipeline PR "Front page sizes").

## Change

- `Projection::reconcileTrends()` stores the payload's `front` as `ProjectionState` `front`. A payload without it leaves what is stored.
- `FrontSizes::read()` checks each value against what the layout carries and falls back to the old amount otherwise:
  - posts under the lead and trends: rows of three;
  - a member: one report band;
  - a visitor: a lead report and up to three beside it.
- `HomeController` uses the sizes for:
  - a member's posts under the lead, trends and report (none hides the band);
  - a visitor's trends and reports.
- A visitor's three posts stay three, because that row is a fixed three-column design.
- `home.blade.php` no longer takes six trends a second time.

## Order

This is safe before or after the pipeline PR: without sizes the pages are as they are now.

## Checked

- `tests/Feature/FrontSizesTest.php`: defaults, sizes applied to both homes, out-of-range values falling back, and the reconcile storing and keeping the sizes.
- Full suite: 430 of 434 pass. The 4 that fail need a built stylesheet or a real checkout (BuildStamp, Icons, Ticker) and fail the same way in any worktree here.

## Since the first draft

- The sizes take any whole number in range, not only a few choices:
  - posts under the lead: 0 to 24;
  - trends: 1 to 24;
  - a member's reports: 0 to 1;
  - a visitor's reports: 1 to 4.
- A live post an editor took off the front page (`off_front_at`, new column, carried by the projection) is skipped on both homes (`Article::onFront`). It stays on /posts. Tests cover both, 21 of 21 in the touched files.
params.title: Home pages show as many posts, trends and reports as the editors set
